given: User holds a valid API token with category creation permissions in header 'Authorization: Token <token>'
InvenTree database is operational with or without existing categories
when: User submits POST /api/part/category/ with a valid name (1-100 characters) and optional parent ID, or submits via the UI 'Add Category' panel
then: System creates the category and returns HTTP 201 Created with the full category object including system-assigned integer ID
When parent ID is omitted or null, category is created as a root-level category with parent: null
When valid parent ID is provided, category is nested under that parent and pathstring reflects the parent lineage
Duplicate category names within the same parent scope are rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request
UI category tree view renders the newly created category in the appropriate node position and displays a success notification
businessRules: Category name is required and non-empty (max 100 characters)
Category names must be unique within the same parent category scope
Write access requires a valid API token in the Authorization header
testabilityRationale: Verifiable via automated REST API POST requests asserting 201 and 400 responses, and Playwright UI tests creating root and nested categories.

given: InvenTree database is populated with multiple root and child categories
when: Client sends GET /api/part/category/ with optional query parameters 'parent=<id>', 'parent=null', or 'ordering=name', or navigates the UI Parts section
then: API returns HTTP 200 OK with a JSON list/envelope containing at minimum id, name, description, and parent_id for each category
Query with parent=<id> returns only direct child categories of that specific category
Query with parent=null returns only root-level categories
List endpoint supports sorting by category name in ascending or descending order
UI renders expandable/collapsible tree nodes, and clicking a category node filters the parts list to that category
businessRules: Response payload must provide hierarchical linkage (parent_id or parent)
Unfiltered category list retrieval must respond deterministically
testabilityRationale: Verifiable via API GET query parameter matrix testing and Playwright UI tree node expand/collapse and filter verification.

given: A Part Category exists with known integer ID, metadata, parent category, and assigned parts
when: Client dispatches GET /api/part/category/{id}/ or selects the category in the Category Tree view
then: Request with a valid numeric ID returns HTTP 200 OK with the full category object including id, name, description, parent, pathstring, and part_count
Response pathstring contains the complete breadcrumb path from root to current category
Response part_count accurately equals the count of parts assigned to this category
Request with an invalid, non-numeric, or non-existent category ID returns HTTP 404 Not Found
UI category detail panel renders the category name, breadcrumb lineage, description, and part count
businessRules: A valid numeric category ID must return HTTP 200; invalid IDs must return HTTP 404
Part count reflects real-time assigned parts
testabilityRationale: Verifiable via REST API GET status and schema assertions for 200 and 404 paths, and Playwright inspection of the detail panel.

given: An existing Part Category exists with ID {id} and user provides a valid write token
when: Client sends PUT /api/part/category/{id}/ with updated attributes (name, parent, description) or modifies the category via the UI 'Edit' action
then: Valid payload returns HTTP 200 OK with the fully updated category object
Renaming a category propagates updated pathstrings to all descendant categories
Attempting to set the parent to a descendant category (circular hierarchy) is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request
Omitting the required 'name' field in a PUT body is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request
UI category tree view immediately updates the category label and hierarchical position, displaying a success notification
businessRules: The name field is mandatory in PUT requests; missing name yields HTTP 400
Circular parent-child hierarchies are strictly forbidden to maintain tree acyclicity
Write operations require valid authentication credentials
testabilityRationale: Verifiable via API PUT requests testing valid renaming, missing fields, circular parent references, and Playwright UI edit interactions.

given: An existing Part Category exists with ID {id} and user holds a valid write token
when: Client dispatches DELETE /api/part/category/{id}/ or triggers category deletion via the UI action menu
then: Deleting an empty category (no assigned parts and no children) succeeds and returns HTTP 204 No Content
Deleting a category with assigned parts is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request unless parts are reassigned or deleted first
Deleting a category with child categories without cascade authorization is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request
Requests without a valid API token return HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 403 Forbidden
UI displays a confirmation dialog before deletion; upon confirmation, category is removed from the tree and success toast appears
businessRules: Categories with assigned parts cannot be deleted; referential integrity prevents orphaned parts
Successful deletion returns HTTP 204 No Content
Write access requires a valid API token
testabilityRationale: Verifiable via API DELETE requests on empty vs populated categories, asserting HTTP 204 and HTTP 400, and Playwright UI confirmation flow.

given: A valid Part Category exists in InvenTree and user possesses a valid write token
when: Client sends POST /api/part/ with part details (name, category, optional IPN, description, flags) or submits the UI 'Create Part' modal
then: Valid payload creates the part and returns HTTP 201 Created with the complete part representation including system-assigned integer ID
New part defaults to active=true if active flag is omitted from creation payload
Payload missing mandatory 'name' or 'category' is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request and field-level validation errors
Payload specifying a non-existent category ID is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request
Payload with duplicate IPN already in use is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request
UI parts list reflects the new part and navigates or links to the new part detail page (/part/{id}/)
businessRules: Part name is required, non-empty, and max 100 characters
Category is required and must reference an existing category foreign key
IPN (Internal Part Number), if provided, must be globally unique across all parts
Write access requires a valid API token
testabilityRationale: Verifiable through API contract tests validating 201 Created, missing mandatory fields, duplicate IPN rejection, and Playwright form submission.

given: Catalogue is populated with parts across multiple categories with active and inactive statuses
when: Client sends GET /api/part/ with optional pagination query parameters 'limit' and 'offset', or loads /part/ in the web browser
then: API returns HTTP 200 OK with a paginated envelope containing count, next URL, previous URL, and results array
Each part object in results includes id, name, description, category (id + name), IPN, active flag, and thumbnail URL
Unfiltered list request returns response within 2,000 ms under standard load (< 50 concurrent users, < 10,000 parts)
Negative limit or offset values return HTTP 400 Bad Request
UI renders parts table with pagination controls matching the API count, next, and previous links
businessRules: Response must provide standardized pagination metadata (count, next, previous, results)
Performance SLA requires response time <= 2,000 ms for unfiltered catalogue list
testabilityRationale: Verifiable via API envelope schema checks, pagination boundary tests, k6 response time benchmarks, and Playwright table pagination checks.

given: A Part entity exists with ID {id} containing metadata, category, IPN, flags, and stock relations
when: Client sends GET /api/part/{id}/ or navigates to /part/{id}/ in the web UI
then: Valid numeric part ID returns HTTP 200 OK with all fields: id, name, description, category, IPN, active, purchaseable, saleable, trackable, virtual, units, minimum_stock, and image thumbnail URL
Non-existent or non-numeric part ID returns HTTP 404 Not Found
UI Part detail page displays all part fields, category link, active badge, and renders tabs for Details, Stock levels, BOM, and Suppliers
businessRules: Valid numeric part ID returns HTTP 200; invalid/non-existent returns HTTP 404
Complete entity representation must be returned in detail view
testabilityRationale: Verifiable through automated REST GET contract tests and Playwright UI tests validating tab rendering on /part/{id}/.

given: An existing Part exists with ID {id} and user supplies a valid write token
when: Client sends PUT /api/part/{id}/ with full part payload or submits the UI 'Edit Part' form
then: Valid complete payload updates all part attributes and returns HTTP 200 OK with the updated part representation
Omitting mandatory 'name' or 'category' field in PUT body returns HTTP 400 Bad Request
Supplying a non-existent category ID returns HTTP 400 Bad Request
Updating IPN to a value already used by another part returns HTTP 400 Bad Request
Boolean flags (active, purchaseable, saleable, trackable, virtual) default to false when omitted from PUT body
UI part detail page immediately reflects updated values and displays a success notification
businessRules: PUT represents a full resource replacement; all required fields must be supplied
IPN must remain globally unique across all parts
Write access requires a valid API token
testabilityRationale: Verifiable via API PUT full-replacement assertions, duplicate IPN error paths, and Playwright edit modal validation.

given: An existing Part exists with ID {id} and user supplies a valid write token
when: Client sends PATCH /api/part/{id}/ with a subset of fields (e.g. toggling active=false or changing description) or uses inline edit affordance in UI
then: System updates only the supplied fields and returns HTTP 200 OK with the complete updated part representation
Unsupplied fields retain their current values without modification
An empty request body ({}) returns HTTP 200 OK with the unchanged part object (no-op)
When active is set to false, part remains accessible via GET but is marked as inactive
If IPN is included in PATCH body, duplicate value check is enforced, rejecting collisions with HTTP 400 Bad Request
UI updates only the modified attribute and displays a success notification
businessRules: PATCH performs partial update; omitted fields must not be overwritten or defaulted
PATCH with empty payload is a valid no-op returning HTTP 200
Write access requires a valid API token
testabilityRationale: Verifiable via API PATCH partial payload tests, empty body tests, active flag toggle verification, and Playwright UI tests.

given: An existing Part exists with ID {id} and user holds a valid write token
when: Client sends DELETE /api/part/{id}/ or selects 'Delete Part' from the UI action menu and confirms
then: Deleting an unreferenced part with zero stock items and no BOM relations returns HTTP 204 No Content
Attempting to delete a part with existing stock items is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request and descriptive error message
Attempting to delete a part referenced as a BOM item in another assembly is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request
Requests without a valid API token return HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 403 Forbidden
UI presents a confirmation dialog before deletion; upon confirmation, user is redirected to /part/ list and toast is shown
businessRules: Parts with active stock items or BOM references cannot be deleted to prevent referential corruption
Successful deletion returns HTTP 204 No Content
Write access requires a valid API token
testabilityRationale: Verifiable via API DELETE assertions across unlocked parts, stock-locked parts, and BOM-locked parts, and Playwright UI confirmation tests.

given: InvenTree catalogue contains parts across multiple categories with distinct active flags, names, and IPNs
when: Client queries GET /api/part/ with combinations of 'category=<id>', 'active=true|false', and 'search=<keyword>', or uses UI filter controls
then: Query with category=<id> returns only parts directly assigned to that category
Query with active=true returns only active parts; active=false returns only inactive parts
Query with search=<keyword> performs case-insensitive substring search matching name and IPN
Combining category, active, and search parameters applies logical AND conjunction (intersection of filters)
Queries with zero matching records return HTTP 200 OK with empty results array (not HTTP 404)
Filtered query responds within 3,000 ms under standard load (< 50 concurrent users, < 10,000 parts)
UI /part/ list table dynamically filters records according to applied filter facets with debounced updates
businessRules: Multiple filters must be evaluated with logical AND conjunction
Zero-match queries must return HTTP 200 with results: []
Filtered query performance SLA is <= 3,000 ms
testabilityRationale: Verifiable via API filter combination test matrices, zero-result assertions, k6 load latency tests, and Playwright interactive filter tests.

given: InvenTree API endpoints for Part and Part Category write and read operations
when: Client dispatches requests with missing, malformed, expired, unprivileged, or valid authentication tokens
then: Mutating requests (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) without Authorization header return HTTP 403 Forbidden or HTTP 401 Unauthorized
Mutating requests with an invalid or expired token return HTTP 401 Unauthorized with descriptive error details
Requests with a valid token belonging to a user without write permissions return HTTP 403 Forbidden
Requests with a valid token supplied in 'Authorization: Token <token>' format succeed with appropriate 2xx response
Tokens never appear in URL query strings, server access logs, or error responses
UI redirects unauthenticated users attempting to access /part/ to the login page
businessRules: All mutating API endpoints must enforce token authentication without exception
Authorization header format must adhere to 'Authorization: Token <token>'
Session cookies must not be accepted for programmatic API write operations
Token secrets must be protected from leakage across logs and error messages
testabilityRationale: Verifiable through automated security API test suite evaluating valid, missing, malformed, and unprivileged tokens across all write endpoints.
